content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Haley Roberts (E021) requests write access to Source Code.

The notes conflict:
- Notes 1-5 (HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities) say she is a full-time Engineer, recommending write.
- Note 6 (Security) says Security DB shows she is a CONTRACTOR with basic security training, recommending read. Note 6's role field says "not looked up in own database" - meaning the security agent didn't verify the role. But they looked up employment type and security training in their own database.

The Security note claims contractor with basic training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training means max is read. Requested write exceeds max, so grant max = read.

However, there's a conflict. Which note to trust? The Security agent looked up employment type in their own database, while other agents relied on team memory (which showed full_time). Actually note 2's employment type "not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1" - so IT didn't verify. Notes 3-5 also didn't verify employment type themselves.

The Security agent is the one who actually verified employment type in their own database, and it found contractor. So the employment type is contractor, basic training.

For Source Code, contractor with basic training: max is read. Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.

But wait - the policy for contractors: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin. So max is read with basic training. Grant read.

Evidence: Security DB (authoritative for employment type/security training) shows contractor with basic training. Other notes relied on team memory without verifying. So the correct decision is read.

Let me submit decision: read.
